- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward or downward trends.
- When prices spike, model reacts with an overshoot followed by a premature correction.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting behavior — fails to recognize that prices often return to prior levels after short-term volatility.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in capturing recent downward trends; model delays recognizing price drops.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility, especially in the last 5–7 days of the forecast window.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then become overly pessimistic in the final 5–7 days.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30-day window — especially around mid-forecast period.
- When true prices are near or below historical mean, model still forecasts higher values.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market interventions — tends to ignore short-term regulatory shocks.
